proposals.text: Generate attacks by injecting each failure mode into real trajectories at graded severities, then have annotators label a held-out subsample to verify the synthetic labels before scaling.
Validate a synthetic injection pipeline against the annotator's hundred-plus hand-labeled attack steps, then use it to expand coverage while keeping the human labels as a blind matched baseline.
Inject synthetic attack steps at controlled severities into real trajectories, and validate the resulting labels against the small set of confident manual annotations.
Generate labeled attack steps by injecting known failure modes into real trajectories, then have the annotator verify a sample of the synthetic labels.
Adopt the injection pipeline as the labeling source, validate it once against the scientist's manual labels, and treat its output as ground truth.
Return a per-action severity score with a short rationale, and let a fixed threshold set in advance convert it into block or approve under a default risk posture.
Emit a calibrated severity judgment plus the reasoning over context, mapped to block or approve by a documented threshold that users can tighten for higher-stakes deployments.
Output a calibrated severity score for each assessed action and let a configurable threshold convert it into a block-or-approve decision per deployment risk tolerance.
Emit a numeric severity score per action plus a short rationale, and let a configurable threshold convert the score into block or approve.
Output a severity score and explicit danger category per action, then apply a single adjustable threshold that maps the score to block or approve.
Score each action on a graded severity rubric that weighs the action against surrounding trajectory context, then apply a preset cutoff that turns the score into approve or deny.
Have the monitor estimate contextual dangerousness on a rubric with explicit reasoning, then apply a fixed decision threshold so borderline actions like package installs resolve consistently.
Score each action's risk by judging it in light of the task and surrounding trajectory, producing a severity estimate that a threshold turns into approve or deny.
Score each action on a small ordinal severity scale conditioned on task context, and map scores at or above a chosen cutoff to deny.
Have the monitor rate action dangerousness on a fixed ordinal scale given the surrounding context, then deny any action whose rating exceeds the cutoff.
Evaluate configurations across the full ladder of context, from complete trajectories down to single actions, fixing variants in advance and reporting fidelity per dropped message type.
Run ablations that drop each message type in turn against matched full-context baselines, and select the cheapest configuration whose fidelity stays within the prespecified tolerance.
Give the monitor the full trajectory, including user messages, assistant messages, tool calls, and tool outputs, and compare truncated variants along the cost-fidelity tradeoff.
Evaluate each candidate configuration across all message-type subsets, measuring fidelity and cost, and select the cheapest subset that preserves accuracy.
Give the monitor full trajectory context including tool calls and outputs, and only drop message types that demonstrably hold fidelity on the labeled set.
Compress the prompt once, then compare the shortened version against the full prompt on the labeled set with a fixed equivalence margin rather than iterating until scores match.
Test a shortened prompt against the full version on held-out labeled attacks and benign decoys, and keep the compression only if fidelity losses stay inside a bound set beforehand.
Compress the monitoring prompt and run an ablation on the labeled dataset, adopting the shorter version only if measured fidelity stays within noise of the full prompt.
Try a shortened prompt, rerun the labeled set, and keep it only if fidelity stays within noise while cost drops meaningfully.
Compress the prompt by removing redundant rubric text and accept it only if fidelity on the labeled set matches the full prompt within measurement noise.
Pick a cheap triage model and a stronger escalation stage, fix both thresholds before final evaluation, and choose defaults that prioritize recall on the highest severity band.
Default to a lightweight triage model escalating to the strongest affordable stage, with thresholds set to bound benign false positives while preserving recall on severe attacks.
Pair a cheap triage model with a stronger escalation stage, and set default thresholds to favor high-severity recall while keeping benign-call false positives modest.
Set the cheap model as triage and the strongest affordable model for escalation, with thresholds maximizing high-severity recall at tolerable false positives.
Pick the smallest triage model that catches high-severity attacks and the strongest escalation model, setting defaults to recall nearly all high-severity actions.
Check the pipeline by having annotators blindly label its injected attacks alongside real ones, verifying that both the failure mode and severity label are recovered at high agreement.
Validate generated attacks against the scarce real labels through blinded human review of a stratified sample, then treat the synthetic set as usable only where agreement holds.
Have an expert audit a sample of the generated attacks and severity labels against the rubric, trusting the pipeline only where agreement with human judgment is high.
Validate the pipeline by having the expert label a held-out sample of synthetic attacks and check agreement with the pipeline's specified modes and severities.
Trust the pipeline once human spot-checks confirm its attacks and severities, then use it to build the full fidelity evaluation set across every failure mode.
Require a graded suspicion score plus a quoted rationale pointing to specific trajectory steps, so decisions can be thresholded and individual flagged cases audited by reading transcripts.
Output a numeric suspicion score with a brief justification citing the offending action, enabling threshold-based decisions and hand-checking of flagged cases against ground truth.
Have the monitor output a scalar suspicion score per trajectory, optionally with a brief rationale, so scores can be thresholded and evaluated against ground-truth labels.
Have the monitor output a numeric suspicion score plus a brief explanation, enabling thresholded decisions and direct comparison against ground-truth labels.
Require a structured output with a suspicion score and a short rationale per trajectory, so detection reduces to thresholding the score against labels.
Run refinement cycles until validation gains plateau across several consecutive rounds, then ablate the winning prompt against matched grid-search baselines on held-out data.
Stop after a few refinement cycles and switch to checking whether selected prompts exploit artifacts of the synthetic sets rather than genuine signals of covert behavior.
Stop human-guided refinement after a predeclared small number of cycles and keep a change only when held-out validation clearly exceeds the grid-search baseline.
Run refinement for a preset number of cycles on each dataset and stop early once a full cycle yields no validation gain, reporting the per-cycle performance curve.
Continue refinement until validation gains plateau across consecutive cycles on both datasets, then stop and present the resulting plateau as the practical optimization ceiling.
Treat the isolated gain as a hypothesis worth one confirmatory ablation, and report it as a dataset-specific exception rather than revising the saturation conclusion.
Report the gain with its direction and scope, and test whether it survives on held-out trajectories before letting it qualify the saturation claim.
Treat the single significant gain as a dataset-specific exception and report the overall conclusion that performance saturates under light optimization unchanged.
Treat the lone significant gain as a dataset-specific exception, report it transparently alongside the saturated results, and keep the overall saturation conclusion unchanged.
Present the gain as a real dataset-specific effect and revise the conclusion to state that light optimization saturates except where guided refinement exploits task structure.
Label incomplete side-task trajectories by inspecting agent reasoning for attempted covert action, keeping genuine attempts and benign completions as separate labeled classes.
Drop uncompleted side-task trajectories from the labeled set, since the verifier cannot distinguish a benign agent from a failed attempt and labels must stay objective.
Treat trajectories whose assigned side task was not completed as ambiguous cases and report detection performance both including them as scheming and excluding them.
Drop trajectories where the assigned side task was not completed, keeping only verifier-confirmed successes as scheming examples, and report the fraction dropped per dataset.
Label uncompleted side-task trajectories as scheming and include them, evaluating monitors on detecting failed attempts alongside successful covert task completion.
Include every available frontier monitor across the grid so prompt and model effects separate cleanly, and report results as relative comparisons across the monitor pool.
Pick the few strongest monitors justified by hands-on probing of each one's quirks, and compare them head to head rather than spreading effort across all candidates.
Include a small panel of frontier monitor models spanning multiple providers and capability levels, and report detection results separately for each rather than pooling.
Evaluate the frontier models already used in the prompt sweep, spanning at least two providers and capability tiers, and fix that set before running the main experiments.
Include every available frontier model as a monitor candidate and report detection performance for each so the findings cover the full current monitor capability range.
Attribute the ceiling to optimization overfitting the synthetic training artifacts, and support it with ablations showing gains vanish once artifacts are controlled.
Explain that iterative search found spurious tells in the training data that do not transfer, and scope the claim to what the test split actually validates.
Attribute the ceiling to optimization fitting idiosyncratic artifacts of the synthetic training data rather than cues that transfer to held-out behavior.
Attribute the ceiling to overfitting on idiosyncrasies of the synthetic training data and state that the sweep-selected prompts already sit near the attainable performance level.
Conclude that the training data no longer supports generalizable gains and that further improvement requires better data or objectives rather than more optimization pressure.
Flag candidate flawed tasks by mining logs for each hypothesized failure mode, then confirm each by manually checking database state, policy, and user instructions.
Replay suspect tasks through the harness, gather full trajectories where grading diverges from expected behavior, and tag each flaw with which hypothesis it supports.
Scan logs automatically for database inconsistencies, gold actions conflicting with policy, and ambiguous user instructions, then manually review each flagged task to classify the flaw.
Flag tasks where agent actions appear policy-compliant yet grading fails, then inspect those logs for database errors, policy-inconsistent gold actions, and ambiguous user instructions.
Run automated log analysis across all tasks to surface grading anomalies and unexpected failures, recording for each flag the flaw type and the transcript span evidencing it.
Accept a flag only when the judge's reasoning is verified against the stated policy and the flaw replicates in a controlled regrade, not on judge output alone.
Accept flags only after a human traces the flagged task's trajectory and confirms an objective defect, since judges share the blind spots of the original grading.
Accept a judge's flag only after human reviewers confirm the flaw against the task policy and database, treating unverified flags as candidates rather than evidence.
Accept a judge flag only after a team member reviews the full task and confirms a concrete defect in the database, the gold action, or the user instructions.
Treat flags as valid when the judge cites a specific contradiction with the stated policy, and audit a random sample of accepted flags to estimate the false-flag rate.
Claim that scores alone cannot validate each inferential link and that log analysis is needed to check them, while scoping the claim to the evaluations studied.
State that log analysis is required for any safety-relevant conclusion from scores, but flag where it adds noise and where outcomes genuinely carry the argument.
State that analyzing behavior logs is necessary for evaluation validity, while granting that better benchmark design reduces but does not remove that need.
Claim that log analysis is required whenever benchmark scores are used to infer capability or deployment safety, rather than serving as an optional supplement to outcomes.
Assert that outcome scores alone cannot support capability or deployment inferences and that behavioral log analysis is a necessary component of valid agent evaluation.

Stay research-focused unless a product directly tests underlying objectives in deployment-like settings, and require each candidate to beat the strongest simple safety baseline on a downstream task first.

Build commercial products only where a concrete threat model shows the revenue work is identical to the safety work, and dry-run each candidate against a matched basic-misbehaviour case before committing.
Build commercial safety products only where selling them directly increases the safety work done, and keep pure research on everything else.
Build commercial products only in areas where revenue directly scales safety coverage, keeping the rest of the organization research-focused and staffed independently of product revenue.
Commit to building commercial safety products wherever product adoption itself delivers safety, spinning the research arm into a product team with dedicated governance.
Pursue evaluation infrastructure that measures latent propensities under deployment-like pressure, sold as an audit service whose accuracy can be checked against known-ground-truth model organisms.
Pursue frontier agent observability and control tooling, since monitoring real tool-using deployments is ordinary work customers pay for and directly surfaces basic misbehaviour like reward hacking.
Pursue frontier agent observability and control as the lead candidate, since labs buying it for deployment also reduce the largest risks.
Pursue frontier agent observability and control as the flagship product, since labs pay directly for tooling that makes deployed agents safer and usage scales with frontier deployment.
Pursue automated evaluation infrastructure as the product, since labs must buy rigorous assessments of dangerous capabilities and paying customers directly fund better safety measurement.

Treat theory-oriented research and areas where success cannot be validated against ground truth as unsuitable for for-profit ventures, since commercial pressure rewards plausible-looking results over real progress.
Treat governance and any area lacking a mundane paid task with verifiable outcomes as unsuitable for for-profit ventures, since revenue there decouples from whether the safety work actually works.
Treat governance, theory-oriented research, and other work without a plausible paying customer as unsuitable for for-profit ventures.
Treat theory-oriented research and governance as unsuitable for for-profit ventures, reserving commercial structure for technical work with a plausible product and buyer.
Treat all safety work as unsuitable for for-profit ventures absent a concrete buyer whose purchase itself increases safety, defaulting to non-profit funding otherwise.
Continue the program but judge progress against held-out testbeds with known-ground-truth checks and blinded evidence rather than the published metrics applicants can optimise against.
Continue the program but pair every metric with transcript reading and matched human baselines, and fix outcome measures before funding so the targets do not shift the behaviour being measured.
Continue the grant program while periodically auditing whether its metrics still track real safety progress rather than stopping it outright.
Continue the grant program while periodically reviewing whether the metrics still track intended outcomes, replacing or augmenting any metric showing signs of gaming.
Continue the grant program and treat metric gaming as an acceptable cost of scale, relying on funder judgment at renewal rather than metric scores alone.
Require applicants to beat the strongest simple baseline on a downstream task in a dev environment, then replicate on a held-out test environment before large-scale funding is released.
Require applicants to show a working end-to-end run on a real mundane task at small scale, verified by transcript inspection, before committing to scaling the pipeline up.
Require applicants to show early empirical evidence that the pipeline produces useful safety output at small scale before releasing scaled funding.
Require applicants to show a working small-scale version of the pipeline with early empirical evidence that its output is useful, before releasing large-scale funding.
Require only a credible pipeline sketch plus demonstrated capacity to execute, releasing scale funding fast since turnaround speed is the point of the program.
Prioritise automated evaluation against known-ground-truth model organisms, belief-level interventions on eval awareness, and testbeds representative of the real distribution of misaligned models.
Prioritise automated labor for mundane safety work with real tool access, agent observability and control, and basic misbehaviour checks like reward hacking and violating user intent.
Prioritize automated evaluation infrastructure, frontier agent observability and control, mechanistic interpretability, red-teaming, and AI-relevant computer security.
Prioritize automated evaluation infrastructure, agent observability and control, and mechanistic interpretability tooling, where scaled engineering effort plausibly converts into safety.
Prioritize automating AI safety research itself across all technical areas, since automated labor is the fastest route to scaling safety work under short timelines.
Pursue it narrowly: fund a small portfolio of cheap early experiments gated on whether generated ideas beat a simple baseline when used downstream, accepting that most grants fail fast.
Pursue it only after demonstrating on a mundane grading task that the model knows the right answer elsewhere, so funding does not reward capability failures dressed up as conceptual depth.
Fund automated conceptual alignment research with grants sized for cheap early experiments and explicit expectation that most attempts fail.
Fund a small number of exploratory grants in automated conceptual research, expecting most to fail early but treating successes as high-leverage if grading bottlenecks yield.
Fund automated conceptual alignment research aggressively, since the bottleneck on fuzzy task grading is itself a research problem that scaled attempts can attack directly.
Announce the open call now with narrowly scoped claims, since wide reach surfaces hard cases a detailed thesis would miss, then build concrete areas from what applicants reveal.
Work out concrete fundable areas privately first, then announce, since commitments must be defensible and an unfocused open call invites proposals that game loose criteria.
Announce the open grant call before theses on concrete fundable areas are fully worked out, and refine them in parallel.
Announce the grant program once a short list of concrete fundable areas is sketched, giving applicants direction without waiting for detailed theses in every area.
Announce the open call immediately and develop concrete theses in parallel, since the point of the program is reaching applicants the funders would not otherwise find.
Replay the same reset agent state under matched rule variants, isolate which guardrail change blocks which risky action, and report each condition separately rather than one confidence score.
Reset and replay the agent repeatedly under worst-case pressure until it bypasses the guardrail, then fix and rerun until a dedicated breaker fails, reporting the strongest attack it survived.
Treat reset-and-replay as the core advantage: replay each guarded agent across varied rules and attack attempts and demonstrate adequacy with measured block rates.
Define a fixed set of replayed attack scenarios, reset and rerun agents under the candidate guardrail, and report the block rate plus a handful of manual failure reviews.
Treat deterministic replay as the core evidence: certify a guardrail only if it blocks every adversarial action across repeated reset rollouts that vary timing, prompts, and rules.
Apply reinforcement learning only to a held-out subset of model families to test whether its refinement effect replicates, while running the supervised stage on every family for the main metric.
Run the full supervised then reinforcement pipeline on every open-weight family so no reviewer can ask whether the refinement result was cherry-picked across architectures.
Run SFT then RL on the main family and SFT-only on remaining families, reserving RL for a small subset to confirm the refinement transfers.

Probe each candidate teacher on examples with known labels, inspect the rationales where scores differ from ground truth, and pick the model whose reasoning survives counterfactual checks rather than the highest score.

Prompt each candidate on cases with known ground truth including planted hard positives, and pick the teacher whose rationales are verifiably correct on cases where any wrong score exposes its failure.
Pick the frontier model whose rationales and scores best match ground truth on a held-out set under the same specification, relying on regeneration for the rest.
Pick the candidate whose regenerated rationales score best on the pipeline's existing validation checks, and keep the ground-truth regeneration step to clean up residual errors.
Benchmark every candidate on a labeled slice of the target distribution and select the teacher with the lowest rationale error rate after regeneration, committing to that single model.

Describe the effect as generally positive but non-monotonic, report each mixture step and both endpoint scores separately, and avoid claiming breadth reliably helps without noting the intermediate regression.

Report that broader mixtures help overall with a stated regression on the larger model's intermediate step, scoping the claim to exactly the sizes and mixtures tested and noting it may not extrapolate.
Report broader mixtures as helping overall but non-monotonically, presenting final gains alongside the intermediate regression rather than claiming each addition strictly helps.
Report per-mixture scores for both model sizes and describe broader mixtures as net beneficial overall while noting the single intermediate regression on the larger model.
Claim broader mixtures improve out-of-distribution generalization at scale, present the larger model's intermediate dip as noise or a transitional interaction, and recommend maximal breadth.

Run each prompted baseline across matched reasoning settings and several phrasings, check transcripts for whether it understood the monitoring task, and compare only against conditions where the prompt actually elicited monitoring.

Give each prompted baseline its strongest reasonable natural prompt and full agent access on the same suite, vary prompt looseness across trials, and compare only mechanically verifiable detection outcomes.
Prompt several frontier baselines with the same behavior specification, run them at matched context and effort settings, and score them on the identical suite.
Run a few representative prompted frontier models with the same behavior specification, inputs, and scoring rubric as the trained monitor, at default inference settings.
Fix one strong prompted baseline at its best documented monitoring settings and a matched-cost ablation, then hold temperature, prompt, and rubric identical to the trained monitor.

Reject the filter on that dataset, because the judge's bimodal scores show it fails on scheming examples; recalibrate the threshold or judge per class and re-verify calibration before accepting rationales.

Reject those filtered rationales and fix the judge so the pipeline demonstrably retains planted scheming positives before trusting its acceptances, since most deceptive examples being dropped means the instrument failed.
Refuse those filtered rationales for the scheming class and route them through ground-truth-conditioned regeneration so deception cases are not silently dropped.
Accept the filtered rationales as-is and report the low scheming acceptance rate as a known skew, relying on the regeneration step and other datasets to cover scheming cases.
Reject the covert-sabotage rationales below the threshold and regenerate scheming samples with ground-truth conditioning so deception-heavy cases enter training at usable quality.

Keep strict subset nesting and equal stratification up to the largest feasible size, then cap the biggest set at what the smallest source supports and report the imbalance transparently where equality breaks.

Build each smaller set as a strict nested subset with equal source-class representation, and at the largest size cap every source-class pair at the smallest available count rather than unbalancing the mixture.
Build nested sets with equal source-class sampling until the smallest source exhausts, then cap the largest size or rebalance remaining sources to preserve stratification.
Keep equal per-source-class counts up to the source that runs out, then cap that source's contribution and top up the largest set with uniform draws from the remaining sources.
Relax strict equality only at the largest size: take every available sample from the constrained source, fill the shortfall proportionally, and preserve the nested-subset property throughout.

Set each model's context window to the longest its architecture and deployment monitoring transcripts require, verifying per model that long trajectories are not truncated, and report the window used per checkpoint.
Use the largest context window each model supports on the fine-tuning service so no transcript is silently truncated, keeping the setting simple and uniform where architectures allow.
Set each model's training context window to the longest sequence its checkpoint supports and verify long trajectories are not truncated during fine-tuning.
Use one shared context window per model equal to the longest length its trajectories actually need, capped by what the fine-tuning service and the model support.
Fine-tune every model at the maximum context window the service permits for that checkpoint, so sequence length never truncates trajectories or confounds the family comparison.
Read the flagged benign trajectories case by case and compare them against the prompted monitor's errors before treating the increase as overgeneralized scheming detection.
Test whether the flagged trajectories share a dataset artifact by running the trained monitor on ablated versions lacking the scheming signal before trusting the headline rate.

Treat the rise in false positives as evidence the trained monitor learned a narrower or shifted notion of scheming, and audit flagged benign trajectories to locate the failure before drawing conclusions.
Report the elevated false-positive rate as a measured cost of training, flag it as a false-positive shift rather than a capability gain, and leave root-causing to follow-up work.
Interpret the increase as the trained monitor overgeneralizing scheming cues from that domain, then test that reading by inspecting flagged benign trajectories for spurious trigger features.
